title: Add, simplify or divide rational expressions
subtitle: Equivalent expressions · 12 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **12 of the official questions in Equivalent expressions are this one** — 0 Easy, 3 Medium, 9 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The expression has a variable in the denominator, often with a note like 'where x > 0' or 'x ≠ some value'.
- You're asked to add two fractions, cancel a common factor, or rewrite a polynomial divided by a binomial as a quotient plus a remainder over the divisor.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) To add or subtract, multiply each fraction to get the common denominator, then combine the numerators.
- 2) To simplify, factor the numerator and denominator and cancel the shared factor (the restriction tells you this is allowed).
- 3) To divide, rewrite the numerator as (divisor × something) + remainder and split it into two fractions, or use long or synthetic division.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph the original and each choice for x in the allowed domain.
The equivalent one overlaps everywhere except possibly at a hole.
This is very reliable when the algebra is messy.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You add numerators and denominators straight across.
Or you cancel a single term instead of a factor that multiplies the whole numerator and denominator, or you lose the remainder term in a division.
